reason: A: the content is pushed low, leaving a large empty band across the top. The jar is shrunk to a small thumbnail. The tiny NEW badge sits alone under the subline at the bottom-left, far from the product, and the CTA floats on the far right with a big gap after the copy. B reads clearly left to right (headline, then a decently sized jar, then the CTA) and is better balanced vertically. Its main flaws are the tiny NEW badge, cut off from the jar and stuck in the top-left corner, and the large empty gaps between the three columns.

A reads left to right (bottle, quote, attribution/logo, CTA) and the CTA is clear. But the quote, which is the headline, is set at about 6px and is barely readable. The large quote mark floats far above it, the attribution sits apart from the quote at top right, and the bottle and its circle are cropped against the left edge. B breaks the design apart: the quote is wrapped into three cramped lines at left, and the quote mark sits after the quote and the bottle instead of before it. The peach circle is cut off at right with no bottle in it. The attribution is tiny low-contrast text tucked next to the CTA, which leaves the reading order jumbled.

A: the $48 price is too small to stand out, and the 'THE NIGHT SET' eyebrow ends up below its own supporting copy. The cream circle is pulled away from the products and cut off at the right edge, the cream jar is tiny and stranded at the bottom centre, and the CTA sits far from the copy with a big empty gap in the middle. B: the logo and $48 are larger and centred, so the hierarchy is better. But the CTA collides with the clipped cream circle, the jar is again tiny and stranded beside the bottle, 'Worth $72' is set bigger than the product line, and the eyebrow is still last; it is marginally less broken than A.

Both break the hierarchy in the same ways. 'THE NIGHT SET' has dropped from eyebrow above the price to below the body copy. 'Worth $72…' is set larger than the product description, so the fine print competes with the message. The cream jar is cut off from the serum and stranded under the CTA as a tiny orphan. A also leaves an awkward empty gap between the circle and $48. B pushes the logo into a tiny top-right corner, which weakens the brand, and its bottle spills out of the circle, making a cramped top. A wins narrowly because its logo stays centred and readable.

A has a clear headline and a strong CTA on the right, but the 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow sits below the subhead, which breaks the reading order. The legal text is squeezed into an unreadable sliver jammed against the leaf thumbnail, and the logo and jar are shrunk to near-invisible scraps in the corner. B crops the leaf art to a thin edge strip and shrinks the CTA into a small pill that loses prominence. Its logo, jar and eyebrow are strung along the bottom row as scattered fragments, the eyebrow comes last, and a dense legal block is crammed against the headline at the top right, where it competes with the message.

A: the headline and CTA lead the card clearly and the subhead is readable. But the OBSIDIAN logo has been pulled out of the card and sits small on the busy city image, the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow now falls below its own subhead (wrong reading order), and the card is jammed against the top, right and bottom edges. B: the right earcup of the headphones collides with the card's left edge and the left earcup is crowded at the canvas edge. The subhead and eyebrow are shrunk to an illegible line of fine print at the bottom, and the oversized logo competes with the headline for attention.

A: the date card (SAT 22 NOV, 8PM–1AM, the key event info) is shrunk to an unreadable speck, and the layout is scattered: the CTA floats in the left column away from its copy, the eyebrow, FIZZBANG! logo and headline all sit on different edges, and the controller is tiny next to the body copy. B: it shrinks the date card the same way and wedges it against the art panel, and the bottom row crams eyebrow, copy, CTA, logo and controller together, but the headline dominates cleanly from a shared left edge and the reading order holds, so it's the less broken of the two.

A shrinks the logo pill to a small shape pushed right of centre, the 'FIZZBANG!' wordmark spills past the pill's outline, and the SINCE 2026 badge is crammed near the right edge, leaving the left half as empty halftone. B keeps the original centred stack with a larger logo and the badge under it, but the wordmark fills the pill too tightly and the badge text is small, so it needs polish before it could ship.

A keeps the centred two-line headline in the same proportion as the original and sits it evenly in the landscape frame. It's quiet but true to the minimalist original; the only nit is that it sits a little high and the bottom margin is heavier. B pushes the text block hard to the left edge (about 30px gutter) and leaves the right ~40% as dead space. The 'silence.' line is centred under the first line while the block is left-placed, so it is neither centred nor flush-left and reads as accidental. The block also sits high with a big empty bottom.

A moves the Monograph logo to the bottom-left corner as a tiny afterthought with an illegible 'Gallery' line. That breaks the brand-first reading order and leaves it off the centre axis everything else uses. It also puts the price above the product name and leaves the narrow centre column floating in wide empty sides. B keeps the logo at the top on the centre axis, so the order is brand, product, then CTA. But B's logo is undersized and its 'Gallery' is unreadable, and it shares A's flaws: price above the name and a thin column that ignores the square format, with large dead side areas.

A: the white card covers almost the whole canvas, so the architectural photo is reduced to slivers in the top corners and the original's photo-plus-card split is lost. The 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, breaking the reading order, and the centred CTA clashes with the left-aligned text block and is jammed under the eyebrow. B: the logo sits on the busy photo and the 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark runs across the card edge, an unintended collision. 'GALLERY' has almost no contrast against the image, 'NOW OPEN' is again out of order below the body and oversized, and the headline wraps awkwardly. B's collision and illegible logo text make it worse than A, which is clean but loses the imagery.

A: the white card covers nearly the whole canvas, so the desert dunes and sun are gone and only orange slivers show at the corners. Copy sits about 12px from the left edge and the subline leaves 'June.' orphaned, but the headline, logo and CTA are clear and well grouped in a sensible left-to-right banner. B: keeps the dunes, but the card is cut off at the top and bottom canvas edges, the centred logo doesn't share an axis with the left-aligned copy, and the 'See Fares' CTA has shrunk to an illegible pill, burying the action.

A reads left to right with a clear headline, subline and a properly sized See Fares button. But the Meridian logo is shrunk to a barely legible speck above the CTA, the card runs into the right edge, and the dunes are cut down to a meaningless sliver. B has the logo sitting directly on the busy dune texture, far from the message. Its headline nearly overflows the card, and the CTA is tiny, squeezed to 'SeeFares' (the space is gone) and jammed against the card's bottom edge, so the call to action is buried.

A reads cleanly left to right (logo → headline with its 'Obsidian Buds, $179' subline → product → Shop) and keeps the headline dominant. Its flaws: the logo is jammed against the left edge, the product shot is shrunk to a minor element, and the CTA sits tight to the right edge. B shrinks the price line to illegible micro-text and detaches it from the headline, dropping it under the product shot. Its logo is also tiny and hugs the edge, leaving the headline floating in an unbalanced middle.

A: the headphones are cut off at the left edge, the headline sits jammed against the top, and the 'PICK YOUR SOUND' eyebrow has dropped below the price. The Buds label is now a pill competing with the CTA, the earbuds case has shrunk to a tiny fragment at the bottom, and the logo is pushed into a bottom-left corner next to an empty pedestal ellipse. B: the logo and headline keep their original top-left order, but the left text column is cramped and the body copy runs into the headphone earcup. The eyebrow also sits below the price, and the earbuds case is a cut-off speck at the bottom edge. Still, B's hierarchy and reading flow are closer to the original.

A: the spec grid is broken up and scattered. 250 g and BT 5.4 are unreadably tiny, and BT 5.4 sits on the cropped circle. The tagline and legal text are squeezed into narrow ragged columns beside the CTA, and the headphone circle is cut off at the right edge. B: the specs are also scattered at random sizes (BT 5.4, 40 h and 250 g are tiny), and the tagline and legal text are thin, word-per-line columns. Still, the headphones stay whole, and the headline and CTA form a clear group with the CTA prominent, so B is slightly less broken.

A: the headline is shrunk to roughly the size of the cyan source line, so it barely leads. The quote mark is a speck, 'Rated 5 out of 5' is near-illegible, and the text block floats off-centre with dead space at both ends. Its saving grace is a readable OBSIDIAN logo anchored on the right. B: the logo is shrunk to an unreadable smudge jammed against the left edge, so the brand is effectively lost. The text stack overfills the height: the quote mark touches the top, 'Rated 5 out of 5' sits on the bottom edge, and the line spacing is cramped. There is a big empty gap between the logo and the copy.

A: 'Rated 5 out of 5' has shrunk to unreadable micro-text. The logo sits centred at the top while the quote block is left-aligned at about x=178, so the two use different axes. Putting the logo first also breaks the original reading order, and the right two-thirds of the banner is empty. B: the headline, source line and rating keep a sensible size hierarchy and share a clean left edge. But the logo is centred at the bottom, off that left edge and jammed near the bottom of the canvas. The quote mark floats with a large gap above the headline, and the right half is dead space, so it reads as a left-stacked square layout rather than a real banner.

A is basically a scaled-down copy of the square layout: the headline, CTA, ZERO SUGAR and FIZZBANG text are all too small to read, and the yellow circle has come loose from the can and drifted right, where it reads as a random blob with the NEW FLAVOUR badge stuck to it. There's also a lot of dead blue space. B actually rearranges for the banner: a big left-aligned headline, the logo top-left, and the can on the right with its yellow backdrop. But the Grab a Can CTA is small and gets lost in a row with the NEW FLAVOUR badge (squashed from a circle into a pill) and the ZERO SUGAR tag, so the button and the badges compete. The yellow circle is cropped and barely visible behind the can, and the bottom row is indented and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge.

A: '$3' now sits above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards, and the price shrank from the hero to a small heading. The CTA hangs left of the text column, the FIZZBANG logo is shrunk to a tiny pill stuck in the bottom-right corner, and the can is jammed against the top edge. B has the same reversed '$3 / 2 FOR' order and small price, and it is worse because the 'Find a Store' CTA has shrunk to an unreadable sliver. The logo is a tiny pill crammed next to it under the text, which buries the CTA and the brand, and the right third of the canvas is dead space.

A: the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill with near-illegible text and pushed to the bottom-left, so it is buried. The flavour list is out of the original order, set in shrinking sizes and staggered diagonally so no edge lines up, and it floats in the middle with dead blue space around it. B: the headline still wraps to leave an orphaned 'sugar.', and the list has the same diagonal stagger, reorder and shrinking sizes, with Lime Zap jammed near the bottom edge. The logo is demoted to a small pill on the far right, sitting next to the CTA. Still, B's CTA and list text are readable and the three columns use the banner better than A does.

A puts the CTA in the top-left, ahead of the headline and the logo, which breaks the reading order. The logo is pushed to the top right, the list is crammed under the headline with shrinking font sizes and drifting dots, and the list order is changed. The bottom quarter of the canvas is empty. B has a sensible top-to-bottom flow (logo, can, headline, list, CTA), but the logo is tiny and sits off-centre. The flavour list shrinks item by item with ragged, staggered dots, is out of the original order, and is cramped under the headline. The CTA text is small and there is a dead band at the bottom.

A has a clean vertical flow: a strong 3-line headline, an evenly spaced and left-aligned flavour list, a centred can and a CTA anchored at the bottom. Its flaws are the reordered list (Cherry, Mango, Cola, Grape, Lime instead of the original order), a FIZZBANG! logo pill shrunk to near-illegibility, and a tight left margin on the list. B has the same reordered list and tiny logo, and it is worse: its bullets are ragged (the Cola, Grape and Lime dots and labels sit at different x-offsets than Cherry and Mango), the list is jammed right under the headline with almost no gap, the headline runs close to both canvas edges, and the CTA button is small and weak.

A: the headline wraps and leaves 'sugar.' alone on the second line. The flavour list is out of the original order, shrinks from item to item and steps off diagonally instead of keeping a shared left edge. The CTA is shrunk to an unreadable pill stuck in the bottom-left corner, with a dead empty area above it. B: the headline fits on one line and the left column holds together better. But B has the same out-of-order, shrinking, diagonal list, and its CTA is a tiny, near-illegible pill floating above the can at the top right, which breaks the reading order. Both lose the CTA hierarchy; B is slightly less broken.

A: clear centred hierarchy (headline, then CTA), but the FIZZBANG! logo is shrunk to a near-illegible chip, the white panel runs full height and swallows most of the pop-art shapes, and the left circle and quarter-circle are clipped. B: the logo badge is dumped on top of the pink circle, navy shape and yellow stripe (an unwanted collision), the headline breaks with an orphaned 'can', and the CTA floats off to the right, away from the copy, so the layout looks scattered rather than designed.

A: the white panel bleeds off the top and right edges and covers most of the pop-art shapes. The FIZZBANG badge has been pulled out of the panel and sits on the pink circle, navy quarter-circle and yellow stripe, and the CTA is pushed hard against the panel's right edge. Still, the headline reads cleanly on one line. B has the same off-canvas panel and the same badge collision with the stripe and circle, and it is worse: the headline breaks into two lines with 'can' orphaned on the second line, unevenly centred, which leaves awkward empty space and looks unintentional.

A: the FIZZBANG! logo has been pulled out of the card and blown up so it competes with the headline, sitting on top of the dark circle and yellow shape. The card almost touches the top and right edges, and the CTA is left-aligned under a centred headline, so the card's contents don't share an axis. The headline also wraps to leave 'a can' on its own line. B: it has the same logo problems, made worse because the logo is even larger and almost touches the left edge, and the same 'a can' wrap. But the card bleeds cleanly off the top and right like a deliberate panel, and the CTA is centred under the headline, so the card reads as one finished group.

A sets the headline on one line at a size that fills the strip and reads clearly, which suits a banner. Its flaws: the left margin is a little narrower than the right, so the line looks slightly off-centre, and there is very little space above and below the text. B keeps the original's centred, minimal feel, but shrinks the headline to a tiny size in a sea of empty space, so it is barely readable at the target size and has none of the original's bold presence.

A reads cleanly left to right (badge, jar, headline/sub, CTA) and the hierarchy holds, but the NEW badge is shrunk to an illegible dot jammed against the left edge, the LUMEN & FIG label is unreadable, and a large dead gap separates the copy from the CTA. B leaves about 140px of empty space on the left so the whole composition sits off-balance, and it wedges the tiny, illegible NEW badge under the subline, almost touching the bottom edge, where it reads like a stray fragment instead of a badge tied to the product.

A: the Shop Now CTA has shrunk to a tiny, unreadable pill that sits apart from the product. The NEW badge is detached from the jar, which is very small, and the headline and subline are jammed against the top-left edge with a large dead area in the middle, so the reading order runs headline → empty space → jar → buried CTA. B: it reads left to right in a sensible order (badge, jar, headline, CTA) and the CTA is legible, but the jar's 'LUMEN & FIG' label can't be read at this size, the NEW badge is cramped against the jar and the left edge, and the headline sits a little low and tight against the jar.

A jams the 'Read 2,400 Reviews' button against the 'MAYA R.' attribution, so the two collide, and pins both to the bottom edge. The quote mark floats far above the quote, the bottle is tiny and stranded mid-canvas, and the oversized logo sits on a cropped circle at the right edge. B reads cleanly left to right (logo, bottle, quote, attribution, CTA), but the quote text is small, the attribution is heavy enough to compete with the quote, the quote mark is detached, and the circle is a cropped sliver behind the CTA, which wastes the original's product-circle motif.

A reads left to right with a strong headline and a clear CTA, but the headphones are cut off at the left edge, the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow sits below the subtitle instead of above the headline, and the subtitle is barely legible at this size. B puts the body copy before the headline as a tiny 5-line block at the far left that breaks 'transparency' mid-word, crams the logo and a near-invisible eyebrow under the headline, and leaves the headphones floating in the middle, so the reading order is wrong.

Both turn the card into a full-height panel that hides the city skyline, leaving only a thin strip at the bottom. Both also move the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow below the body copy, which breaks the reading order, and both use an oversized CTA. In A, the logo is tiny, low-contrast and right-aligned, so it doesn't line up with the left-aligned headline, and there is a large dead gap between the headphones and the CTA. B keeps the logo legible and left-aligned with the copy and has tighter vertical rhythm. Its weakness is that the headline and body sit almost against the left edge (about 6px margin).

A: the reading order goes logo, headphones, headline, which works, but the 'Pick your sound' eyebrow sits on the far right after the headline, and the product labels are swapped (the Buds label sits next to the headphones and the One label next to the buds). The buds case has shrunk to two dots, a stray empty grey oval sits at the right, and the CTA is jammed between the two labels. B: is more scattered. The eyebrow drops to the bottom-left below the body copy, the logo is stranded mid-canvas instead of leading, and the 'Obsidian One' label floats under the body copy away from the headphones. The buds are reduced to a tiny mark in the corner, and the CTA and Buds pill stack in the middle with no relation to their products.

A: the headphones are cropped off the left edge, and the teal circle has come away from them to sit behind the right-hand stats column. In that column the stat labels are illegibly tiny and the stats are out of their original order. The legal note is wrapped awkwardly right beside the CTA. Logo, headline and CTA still read in a sensible order. B: the stats are scattered in fragments down both edges, and the logo is jammed between them on the left. The circle has come away from the headphones and now sits behind '6 mics' and the CTA, which is pushed off to the far right. The legal fine print takes the top line, and the tagline is stranded at the bottom, so the reading order and grouping fall apart.

A drops the Pre-order CTA completely. Stat fragments (-38 dB, 6 mics, 10 min, BT 5.4) are scattered on both sides of the headline and headphones, and the logo, tagline and labels are illegibly tiny. B keeps the headline, the headphones and a prominent Pre-order $349 button in a sensible left-to-right order. But B also crams stat fragments along the bottom edge and into the corners (-38 dB, 40h, 250g, 6 mics), they are unreadable and jammed together, and the tagline is microscopic.

A: the OBSIDIAN logo is shrunk to an illegible speck at far left. The quote mark, headline, attribution and rating are stacked tightly in a 90px-tall strip with almost no leading, and the attribution is nearly as heavy as the headline. The whole right half of the banner is empty. B: the logo is legible at the right edge and the attribution and rating share one line, so the headline clearly dominates. But the quote mark is tiny, the left ~20% of the banner is empty, and there is a wide dead gap between the copy and the logo, so the layout still looks pushed to one side instead of spread across the strip.

A stacks the elements, but the logo, headline and Shop button each sit on a different center axis, so they look scattered at random. The headline is small and weak for this canvas, and the right third is dead space. B keeps the original strip as one thin row across the middle, which leaves large empty bands above and below, and the Shop button is crowded against the right edge. Still, B's alignment, hierarchy and brand read stay intact.

A: the 'Grab a Can' CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill floating above the headline, so it is buried and reads in the wrong order. The yellow circle is cut loose from the can and sits as a meaningless dot at the far right, and the can is tiny while the logo, can and badges are spaced unevenly. B: the CTA sits under the headline where it belongs, but the 'NEW FLAVOUR' badge is squashed into an illegible sliver. The FIZZBANG! logo is oversized, competes with the headline and collides with a yellow circle cropped at the right edge, and the left quarter of the canvas is empty.

Both put '$3' above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. A also shrinks the FIZZBANG logo to an unreadable chip in the top-left corner, leaves the CTA floating at the top far from the copy, and puts the subline close to the bottom edge. B shrinks 'Find a Store' to tiny text and squeezes it next to a logo pill that now looks like a second button, with both jammed under the subline in a cramped bottom row while the top and right sit empty. A wins narrowly because its CTA is legible and its price is a clearer focal point.

A is close to a uniform scale of the original, which works here because the aspect ratios are nearly the same. Hierarchy, reading order, logo size and spacing all survive, though it inherits the orphaned 'long.' and the body copy is small. B shrinks the FIZZBANG! logo pill until it is tiny and puts '$3' above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. It also squeezes the body copy into tiny type on one line and inflates the 'Find a Store' button until it competes with the price. On top of that, a large dead gap sits between the copy and the CTA.

A: the CTA is shrunk to an unreadable pill stuck in the bottom-left corner, and the flavour list is reordered and shrinks progressively until Grape Pop and Lime Zap are barely legible, with ragged dot alignment. A large dead area sits between the content and the can, which is cramped against the right edge. B: it reads left to right (logo, headline, list, can, CTA) and the CTA is legible, but the flavour list has the same reordering, tapering sizes and staggered dots, and the logo floats low and disconnected from the headline.

A reads left to right with a strong one-line headline and its CTA grouped under the copy, but the Lumen & Fig logo is shrunk to an illegible speck. The 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow sits below the subcopy, out of reading order, and there is dead space top-right and bottom-right. B has a bigger headline, but the brand logo and a tiny eyebrow are pushed to the bottom under the body copy, which flips the reading order. The CTA floats alone at the far right, cut off from its copy by a large empty gap, and the bottle's dropper touches the top edge, so the layout feels scattered.

A: the Lumen & Fig logo is shrunk to an unreadable speck in the top-right corner, the headline breaks onto a second line with 'skin' left on its own, and the 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' label has dropped below the body copy, so the reading order is wrong. B: the headline fits on one clean line and the logo stays readable, but the label also sits below the body copy, the logo is pressed against the bottom edge, and the bottle is squeezed into a narrow strip on the left that touches the top and bottom of the canvas.

A is just the square layout shrunk into the strip: the headline, logo, step list and CTA are all tiny and unreadable, the elements float in a scattered diagonal with large empty bands, and the jar has come off the pink circle at the far right. B has a strong left-to-right banner structure with a legible logo, a dominant headline, the jar and a clear CTA, but the four steps are torn apart into unreadable fragments in the corners, in the wrong order (2 and 4 on the left, 1 at top centre, 3 at bottom), and the circle is cut off by the right edge. That leaves B broken, but much less broken than A.

A: the jar is pushed against the left edge. The NEW badge has shrunk to an illegible dot stranded under the subhead, and the small CTA floats at the far right with a big dead gap in the middle. The headline is undersized for the format, and the subhead text is tiny. B: the jar has proper margin and the three columns (product, copy, CTA) read left to right, so it is better balanced. But the NEW badge is again a tiny unreadable dot, now separated from the product and placed near the CTA. The headline is weak, there is a large gap between the headline and the subhead, and the subhead is too small to read.

A has an unwanted collision: the 'Read 2,400 Reviews' button sits right against 'MAYA R., VERIFIED BUYER' on the same baseline, and the quote mark floats far above the headline. The left ~150px is empty, and the logo sits on a cropped circle that has drifted away from the bottle it used to frame. B reads left to right with even spacing (logo, quote, bottle, CTA), but the attribution is set nearly as large as the headline, which weakens the hierarchy. Its bottle has also lost its circle backdrop, and the CTA overlaps the circle cropped at the right edge.

A: the CTA, a tiny jar thumbnail, the logo and the 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow are jammed into one cramped bottom row, so the eyebrow ends up last in the reading order. The leaf image is cut down to a thin strip, and the dense legal block is so large it competes with the headline on the right. B: the headline and CTA hierarchy reads better, but the Lumen & Fig logo and jar shrink to near-invisible specks crushed against a tiny, low-contrast, unreadable legal block. The eyebrow sits below the subhead, the leaves are pushed into a sliver at the far edge, and a dead gap sits in the middle, so B loses more of the brand.

A: the headline-led banner flow and the large CTA work, but the brand logo is shrunk to an unreadable speck at the far right, the jar is a tiny chip, the 'Clinically Tested' eyebrow sits below the subcopy, and the legal block is crammed into illegible micro-text. B: the CTA is shrunk to a tiny illegible pill and loses all prominence, the left ~20% of the canvas is dead space, the leaf image is jammed against the right and bottom edges, and the jar, CTA and logo are lumped together in a cramped row with unreadable legal text.

A keeps the circle round and the logo lockup over the tagline intact, but it just centres the square composition on the landscape canvas, leaving large empty side bands, and the tagline is small. B stretches the circle into a distorted ellipse that is clipped at the top edge, and it shrinks the brand lockup into a tiny corner mark, so the tagline becomes the hero and the original hierarchy is lost.

A keeps the headphone-in-circle art and a clear CTA, but the OBSIDIAN logo is shrunk to an unreadable speck in the bottom-right corner (a brand failure). The $349 price floats centred above the headline with no link to it or the CTA, and a large dead gap separates the copy from the button. B is worse: the teal circle and the headphones are pulled apart, leaving an empty disc on the far left. The copy is broken up, with the body text cut off from its headline and stranded on the far right, the price floating apart from everything, and the CTA jammed next to the logo mid-banner. There is no clear reading order.

Both separate the teal circle from the headphones, so the backdrop ends up stranded in the bottom-left corner behind the logo. Both put the price above the headline, mix a centered price and product with left-aligned copy, and shrink the subhead and Pre-order button until they are tiny. A at least keeps the CTA centered and clear of other elements. B shoves the Pre-order button into the bottom-left corner, overlapping the stray circle and crammed against the logo, and leaves a large empty band at the top.

A reads left to right (logo, headline and price block, then the product as the hero, then Shop), but the logo and the price line are tiny, the earbud case is so large that it competes with the headline, and the Shop button floats in a big empty right zone with uneven gutters. B shrinks the product to a small icon jammed against the left edge, strands the logo alone at top centre away from the headline, and leaves a loose gap between the headline and the tiny price line, so the layout feels like scattered fragments with weak hierarchy.

A: the 'PICK YOUR SOUND' eyebrow has dropped to the bottom under the body copy, so it reads in the wrong order. The 'Obsidian One, $349' caption sits under the body text, far from the headphones it names, and the earbuds image is gone, leaving the 'Obsidian Buds' label orphaned. The layout still runs left to right, with the CTA at the right end and the headphones intact. B: the headphones are cropped at the top and bottom edges, and the earbuds are replaced by an empty grey ellipse that leaves dead space on the right. Both price captions, the CTA, the dots and a tiny eyebrow are crammed into one cluttered row of very small text under the headline, so the CTA gets lost and the eyebrow ends up last.

A breaks up the spec grid into lone stats scattered down the strip in the wrong order, with '10 min' below the CTA. It puts the fine-print disclaimer, set as large as body copy, between the headline and the product. The tagline and stats sit on the teal circle, which is cut away from the headphones. B is also broken: the stats are scattered, the circle sits behind the top text and the tagline, and the disclaimer stays oversized with '6 mics' left alone at the bottom. Its order of headline, product, then CTA reads more naturally, so it is slightly less bad.
